name: Salesforce MCP
tagline: Query and update Salesforce records from your AI agent.
shortDescription: The Salesforce MCP server. Run SOQL queries, manage leads, contacts, opportunities, and accounts, pull reports, and trigger flows. The canonical way to give an agent access to Salesforce.
longDescription:
## What it is

The official Salesforce MCP server. Exposes the Salesforce REST and SOQL APIs as MCP tools: run SOQL queries, CRUD records across standard and custom objects, manage opportunities, pull reports, and trigger flows.

## Why we recommend it

If your org runs on Salesforce, this is the cleanest way to let an agent help. The agent can run reports, update records, and trigger workflows — without anyone logging into Salesforce.

## When to use it

- Reporting: agent runs SOQL, builds a report, returns results
- Data updates: agent updates hundreds of records matching a query
- Lead routing: agent assigns new leads based on rules
- Workflow triggers: agent kicks off a flow when a record changes
installInstructions:
1. Create a connected app in Salesforce (Setup → App Manager)
2. Enable OAuth scopes: `api`, `refresh_token`, `offline_access`
3. Set `SALESFORCE_CLIENT_ID`, `SALESFORCE_CLIENT_SECRET`, `SALESFORCE_USERNAME`, `SALESFORCE_PASSWORD`
4. `npx -y @salesforce/mcp`
pricingDetails: Free. The MCP server is open source. Salesforce has a free Developer Edition org for testing.
